title: CI never builds or tests on the mandated Swift 6.4 / Xcode 27 toolchain
evidence: grep -niE 'xcode-select|DEVELOPER_DIR|setup-xcode|maxim-lobanov|Xcode' .github/workflows/swift-ci.yml -> no match; job runs-on: macos-26 with name 'macOS 26 / Swift 6.3.3+ SwiftPM'. Swift/check-toolchain.sh:4-5 sets minimum_swift=6.3.3, minimum_xcode=26.6, so a 6.3 runner passes. Local mandated toolchain: 'Apple Swift version 6.4 (swiftlang-6.4.0.34.1)', 'Xcode 27.0 (27A266a)'. AUDIT/baseline.md:10-13: on Swift 6.4 the root build FAILED to link (undefined WebTransportTLSCore symbols) so swift test could not run, while CI was green.
expected: The mandated toolchain is the one CI exercises: the macos-swift job selects Xcode 27 / Swift 6.4 (or runs a second matrix leg on it), so a Swift-6.4-only link failure fails a PR.

title: 185 files of CMake/Ninja build output are committed at the repository root
evidence: git ls-files build | wc -l -> 185 (113 .o, 11 .cmake, 3 .dylib, libwebtransport.a, executables); du -sh build -> 4.1M; git check-ignore -v build/CMakeCache.txt -> 'NOT IGNORED: build/'; build/CMakeCache.txt:391 CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY:INTERNAL=/tmp/wt-clone/C99; build/CMakeFiles/CMakeConfigureLog.yaml:23 leaks /Users/andreborchert/...; build/Testing/Temporary/LastTestsFailed.log records '26:test_quic_connection' while ctest today reports '100% tests passed out of 97'. No script, doc or workflow reads build/ (git grep for build/(CMakeCache|build.ninja|tests|apps) in *.sh/*.md/*.py/*.yml returns nothing).
expected: The repository tracks sources only: build/ is untracked and ignored, and build output lives under C99/out/<platform>/ as C99/scripts/build-and-test.sh documents.

title: README says GitHub provides no Windows runner and that the Windows CI job is missing; the workflow runs one on windows-latest
evidence: README.md:51-55: 'runs on two platforms GitHub provides no runner for -- Windows ... and FreeBSD 15.1' and '8 are met and 1 is partial (the CI job for the Windows and FreeBSD legs)'. .github/workflows/c99-ci.yml:261-267 defines windows-native with runs-on: windows-latest (MSYS2 MINGW64, continue-on-error: true), and windows-wine at :213-255 is enforced. c99-ci.yml:6-8 says only 'the FreeBSD leg is still to be added'.
expected: The status paragraph says FreeBSD has no CI leg, and that the native Windows job exists but is not yet enforced.

title: Debian 13 is documented as a green CI platform, but the workflow runs ubuntu-24.04
evidence: C99/README.md:23 '97 CTest tests pass on macOS 26 and on Debian 13'; README.md:50-51 the same. .github/workflows/c99-ci.yml:45-51 matrix is macos-26, ubuntu-24.04 (gcc), ubuntu-24.04 (clang); no Debian leg. c99-ci.yml:5-8 header claims 'macOS 26 and Debian run the tree in CI as they always have' while IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md:2933-2934 names 'Debian 13, GCC' and 'Debian 13, Clang' as the intended legs.
expected: The READMEs and the workflow comment name the platform the matrix actually runs (Ubuntu 24.04), or the Linux legs run in a debian:trixie container.

title: Supported-versions table lists 1.1.x as supported and omits the current 1.3.x line
evidence: SECURITY.md:7-13: 'Security fixes are provided for the current main branch and the latest tagged release line' with table '| main | Yes |', '| 1.1.x | Yes |', '| Earlier releases | No |'. git tag | tail -3 -> 1.3.6, 1.3.7, 1.3.8; README.md:127 pins 'exact: "1.3.8"'. A reader cannot tell whether 1.3.x receives security fixes.
expected: The table names the current release line (1.3.x) and lists 1.1.x under unsupported unless fixes are still issued for it.

title: No secret or dependency/CVE scanning in either workflow, and no scanner configuration for the committed test keys
evidence: grep -niE 'gitleaks|trufflehog|trivy|secret|audit|dependabot|scorecard' .github/workflows/*.yml -> no match; git ls-files | grep -iE 'gitleaks|trufflehog|secret|dependabot|renovate' -> NONE tracked. Full-history scanners (counts only): gitleaks 9 findings over 503 commits (3 private-key in C99/tests/vectors/trust/*-key.pem:1, 6 generic-api-key false positives on Swift enum labels), trufflehog 0 verified / 0 unverified, trivy 0 vulnerabilities / 0 secrets / 12 container misconfigurations. The trust-directory README documents the keys as intentional fixtures, so a CI scanner needs a narrow allowlist.
expected: A CI job runs a secret scanner on every PR with a path/rule allowlist for C99/tests/vectors/trust/, and the system-OpenSSL dependency surface is covered by a vulnerability scan or a written decision not to.

title: Default WebTransportServer invocation prints 'local demo endpoint ready' and exits 0 without binding a socket
evidence: main.swift:95-103 constructs the configuration, does '_ = WebTransportServer(configuration: configuration)' and prints 'WebTransportServer local demo endpoint ready: authority=localhost path=/wt' then returns. WebTransport.swift:429-433 shows init only stores configuration (the doc comment says 'Starts a network listener' on the method, not the initializer). Observed: running .build/arm64-apple-macosx/debug/WebTransportServer with no arguments prints the ready line and exits 0.
expected: The no-argument path either actually listens or reports that no listener was started and exits non-zero, without claiming an endpoint is ready.

title: Three exported C99 functions have no caller and no test anywhere in the tree (SUSPECTED)
evidence: wt_quic_space_name (connection.h:933 / src/quic/connection.c:49), wt_tls_encrypted_extensions_build (tls/handshake.h:166 / src/tls/handshake.c:888) and wt_tls_certificate_verify_build (tls/handshake.h:233 / src/tls/handshake.c:739) each occur exactly twice in the whole C99 tree (declaration + definition). Reachability proof: every file under C99/ except C99/out/ was read and occurrences counted; no test, app, script, CMake or CI reference exists; C has no reflection/registry/string dispatch and the sibling name functions (wt_quic_frame_kind_name, wt_quic_packet_type_name) are called directly from tests; all three are nevertheless exported public API, which is the one legitimate reason to keep an uncalled function, hence SUSPECTED.
expected: Either the functions are exercised by a unit test like their siblings, or they become internal (declaration removed), or they are deleted.

title: Documented C99 check count (91,552) does not reproduce; the measured count is 91,713
evidence: C99/README.md:61 and README.md:48 state '84 test programs and 91,552 checks'. Measured: 'ctest --test-dir C99/out/macos26/build -V' then summing '<name>: all N checks passed' gives 84 distinct programs and 91,713 checks, 0 failures. AUDIT/baseline.md:29 propagated the README figure rather than measuring it.
expected: The README number is the number the suite prints, or the sentence gives an approximate figure ('over 91,000 checks').

title: Three C99 CLI mains still describe the Phase-0 stub that 'prints its usage and exits 3'
evidence: wt-client-c99/main.c:1-8, wt-server-c99/main.c:1-8 and wt-conformance-c99/main.c:1-8 all say the tool is a Phase-0 stub and 'until they do the tool prints its usage and exits 3'. Observed: wt-client-c99 with no arguments exits 2 with 'wt: no address: pass host:port'; --help exits 0; wt-server-c99 behaves identically. The tools are implemented (Phase 9).
expected: The header describes the current tool and its exit statuses (0 success, 1 scenario failure, 2 argument error, 3 nothing failed but something was not attempted).

title: Fuzz test comment says 'CI uses the default' but CI sets a 20,000-iteration budget
evidence: PeerInputFuzzTests.swift:21-23: 'WEBTRANSPORT_FUZZ_ITERATIONS raises the per-parser budget for longer local runs; CI uses the default.' The code default is 400 (line 147). .github/workflows/swift-ci.yml:96-101 sets env WEBTRANSPORT_FUZZ_ITERATIONS: "20000" for the AddressSanitizer fuzz job.
expected: The comment says CI raises the budget to 20,000 under ASan and the default applies to a local swift test.

title: Neither workflow declares permissions: and every action is pinned to a mutable tag
evidence: grep -n 'permissions' .github/workflows/*.yml -> no match in either file. Uses: actions/checkout@v6 at swift-ci.yml:21,90,108 and c99-ci.yml:54,218,273; msys2/setup-msys2@v2 at c99-ci.yml:276. The same workflows pin the MSYS2 OpenSSL package explicitly to avoid moving under the project's feet (c99-ci.yml:170-183), so the principle is already accepted for artifacts but not for actions.
expected: permissions: contents: read at workflow level, and actions referenced by full commit SHA with the tag in a comment.

title: The six interop Docker images run as root and declare no health check
evidence: trivy fs --scanners vuln,secret,misconfig . reports 2 misconfigurations for each of C99/tests/interop/client/Dockerfile:11, C99/tests/interop/peer/Dockerfile:6, C99/tests/interop/peer/Dockerfile.aioquic:2, Swift/interop-docker/pywebtransport/Dockerfile:1, Swift/interop-docker/quiche/Dockerfile:1 and Swift/interop-docker/quinn/Dockerfile:1: DS-0002 (HIGH) no non-root USER and DS-0026 (LOW) no HEALTHCHECK (6 HIGH + 6 LOW total). These are test-only interop containers, but no file records that as an accepted decision.
expected: Test images add a non-root USER where possible, and DS-0002/DS-0026 are either fixed or recorded as accepted for test-only images in a scan policy.

title: Generated badge data is committed and never regenerated by any workflow
evidence: .github/traffic.json holds a fixed snapshot ({ "schemaVersion": 1, "label": "Views (14d)", "message": "18", "color": "blueviolet" }). README.md:11 points an img.shields.io/endpoint badge at it on main. git grep -n 'traffic.json' over the tree returns only that README line: no workflow, script or hook writes the file.
expected: A scheduled workflow refreshes the file, the badge is removed, or the file states it is refreshed by hand and when.

title: --timeout-ms is unvalidated in the Swift server CLI while the C99 CLI rejects the same value
evidence: main.swift:165-170 parses --timeout-ms with Int32(arguments[index]) and stores it with no range guard (the --max-sessions branch at :177-186 is range-checked, so the omission is specific). C99/src/cli/options.c:220-221 rejects a zero timeout with 'a zero timeout would wait forever'. Downstream, WebTransportInteroperableNetworkRuntime.swift:1950-1952 throws WebTransportNetworkRuntimeError.timeout(0) for any non-positive value, so an operator sees a timeout instead of an argument error.
expected: A non-positive --timeout-ms is rejected at parse time with a specific argument error in both space-separated and = forms.

title: The nested Swift manifest is built but its tests are never run, and its smoke executables are never executed
evidence: swift-ci.yml builds 'swift build --package-path Swift' (:41-44) but every test invocation targets the root manifest ('swift test' :74, '--sanitize=address' :100, '--sanitize=thread' :118); 'swift test --package-path Swift' appears nowhere. Swift/Package.swift:132-171 declares LibrarySmokeServer/LibrarySmokeClient executables that no workflow, script or test runs (grep for the names outside the manifest finds only their own sources and same-named structs in WebTransportLibrarySmoke.swift). check-manifest-sync.sh covers shared-target drift only.
expected: CI runs the nested manifest's test configuration (or documents that it is redundant), and the smoke executables are either executed by a script/test or removed.

title: check_spikes_absent cannot fail: neither manifest declares the spike targets it looks for
evidence: build-release-apple-silicon.sh:16-24 rejects AppleQUICSpike/NativeQUICCoreSpike found in the release output, and calls it at :89-90 and :111. The script builds only via 'swift build -c release --arch arm64 --product WebTransportClient|WebTransportServer' (:62-67), and SwiftPM builds only declared targets; grep for AppleQUICSpike in Package.swift and Swift/Package.swift returns nothing, and Swift/Experiments has no Package.swift. The invariant is separately asserted where it can fail, by the release-products conformance scenario reading the manifests (WebTransportCLIConformance.swift:736-753).
expected: The guard is deleted (the manifest-level conformance scenario owns the invariant) or reworked to inspect the resolved build plan so it can actually observe a spike target.

title: No third-party licence notice for OpenSSL, the C99 build's REQUIRED dependency
evidence: LICENSE is MIT. C99/CMakeLists.txt:38 does 'find_package(OpenSSL 3.0 REQUIRED)' and the build produces install/package artifacts (libwebtransport.0.1.0.dylib and the install rules), so an Apache-2.0 dependency's notice must be retained on redistribution. git ls-files | grep -iE 'notice|third.?party|license|copying' returns only LICENSE, C99/third_party/.gitkeep (empty directory) and two interop shell scripts; no NOTICE/THIRD_PARTY file exists and no doc mentions the OpenSSL licence.
expected: A THIRD_PARTY notice naming OpenSSL, its version floor and its Apache-2.0 licence, referenced from the install/package rules.
